Dependence Reconfiguration: How Supply-Side Constraints Reshape Demand-Side Innovation

With Tony W. Tong and Yuping Li

Working paper

Concentration of critical technologies

Firms in the Global South often depend on a small set of Global North incumbents for critical upstream technologies.

When governments use technology access in geopolitical competition, that dependence becomes a vulnerability.

ASML 2024 annual report; TrendForce 2024; SemiAnalysis 2025; Gartner 2024

Technology sanctions further constrain development

ZTE 2018

An April 2018 BIS denial order cut off all U.S. technology inputs, including Qualcomm chips and Google Android licensing. ZTE halted its main operations within weeks.

Russia 2022

Sweeping U.S. and EU export controls after the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine cut Russia off from Western semiconductors, computers, telecom and dual-use technology.

Iran since 1995

U.S. executive orders (1995) and the Iran Sanctions Act (1996) restricted trade and technology, including advanced semiconductors, encryption software and internet infrastructure.

Cuba (since 1962) · South Africa (1977–1994) · North Korea (since 2006) · Venezuela (since 2017) · Myanmar (since 2021)

The puzzle

The U.S. cut these firms off from advanced chips, yet many of them opened their code. Why?

This paper

Research question

When a critical upstream technology is restricted,
how do firms organize their innovation from downstream?

We study how an environmental supply constraint changes how firms organize innovation: from concentrated supply-side dependence on a few players to distributed demand-side dependence on many users and developers.

Preview: 664 Chinese software firms, matched difference-in-differences, 2020–2025.
Our sample is the broader AI software sector, mostly application firms.

Related literature

Two levels of dependence

How can firms sustain innovation when access to critical inputs is restricted not by any single partner, but by an across-the-board supply constraint?

Partner level. Dependence arises from a specific exchange relationship and can be addressed by altering the terms of that relationship or by seeking alternative partners.

Environmental level. Dependence arises from how a critical resource is distributed across the entire field of potential suppliers. Switching partners does not resolve asymmetry. Global South firms often face this kind: critical upstream technology is concentrated among a few Global North incumbents.

October 2022 was of the second kind: every frontier supplier fell under the same rule at once.

Upstream after October 2022: high power imbalance. Firms needed the chips and had no equivalent supplier; the supplier did not need them in the same way. Power imbalance: the asymmetry in how much each party needs the other (Casciaro & Piskorski 2005).

Traditional responses, blocked

“Traditional resource dependence theory typically directs firms’ response strategies toward the supply side of the exchange. … In the context of the U.S. export controls, however, none of these responses was available or feasible for Chinese AI firms.”Liu, Tong & Li (working paper)

Blocked

1 Absorption (acquire the supplier)

Cross-border acquisitions and alliances within the restricted domain fell under the same controls.

No equivalent

2 Countervailing (turn to an alternative supplier)

All potential suppliers of the restricted hardware fell under the same rule, so firms had no equivalent supplier to switch to. Downgraded chips and workarounds helped only at the margin.

Not viable

3 Avoidance (exit the exchange)

Exiting would mean giving up AI development altogether, the core of what these firms do.

Every route ran into the same rule. So what did firms do?

Hardware and software as complements

LayerBefore Oct 2022After
HardwareAI chips, advanced fabricationfrontier chips on the marketfrontier chips closed by export controls
Cloud computingtraining and inference at scalefrontier compute at homefrontier compute scarce; downgraded chips and renting abroad at the margin
AI modelsthe adjustment marginclosed development pays: the inputs are thereclosed code loses its complement; open release costs less
AI applicationsuser-facing products and servicesvalue from adoption, deployment, monetizationvalue can still be captured once the code is free

Teece (1986) logic, our application: without the complementary asset, frontier compute, keeping code closed returns less.

The demand-based view

Adner & Zemsky (2006), Strategic Management Journal

Competitive advantage depends not only on a firm’s supply-side resources but also on how effectively the firm connects with heterogeneous customers on the demand side.

Priem (2007), Academy of Management Review

Supply-side and demand-side sources of advantage can be distinct; when the former is restricted, value creation may still proceed through the latter.

Our core argument: when the supply of hardware complement is constrained, firms shift strategic emphasis toward the demand side of the technology stack.

There, software value arises through the engagement of users and developers who adopt, adapt, and build upon it.

Dependence reconfiguration

Before: concentrated supply-side dependence on a few players
After: distributed demand-side dependence on many outsiders

Why users innovate

four papers in the von Hippel line

  • 1986Lead usersvon Hippel, Management Science
  • 1994Sticky informationvon Hippel, Management Science
  • 2003Heterogeneous needsFranke & von Hippel, Research Policy
  • 2011Open collaborative innovationBaldwin & von Hippel, Organization Science

Why outsiders contribute: contributing itself pays, through use, learning and reputation.

For a compute-constrained AI firm, the scarce knowledge is how to make models run cheaply on specific hardware, data and languages. Users have it.

Open source and export rules

Export Administration Regulations, 15 CFR § 734.3(b)(3)

Information and software that “are published, as described in § 734.7” are “not subject to the EAR.”

§ 734.7(a)(4): published includes “posting on the Internet on sites available to the public.”

Unlike semiconductors and chips, published code cannot be easily restricted by governments.

Baseline hypothesis: open source project release

1 Complementarity

When the upstream hardware complement is constrained, the channel through which software realized value with that hardware is restricted.

Milgrom & Roberts (1990); Shapiro & Varian (1999)

2 Demand side

Value creation may still proceed through the users and developers who adopt, adapt, and build upon the software.

Adner & Zemsky (2006); Priem (2007)

3 Open source release

Each release opens a new channel through which the firm engages distributed downstream actors.

Lerner & Tirole (2005); Lin & Maruping (2022)

Baseline HypothesisFollowing supply-side constraints on access to upstream hardware complement, software firms will increase open source project release.

Measure, new repository creation: the firm’s monthly count of newly created, non-fork repositories.

Release is the first step. Whether it engages a broad and active community depends on governance: breadth and depth.

Governance: breadth and depth

Breadth: license permissiveness
Depth: gatekeeping openness

Who may use the code, and on what terms

Who holds write access and decides what goes in

GPL v2 · AGPLrestrictive

MIT · BSD · Apache 2.0permissive

Closed gatekeepingonly employees hold write access

Open gatekeepingoutsiders hold it too

Lowers the power imbalance

Deepens mutual dependence

“the rules and structures that determine what outside actors can do with the code and how much influence they have over a project’s development”

Governance, in our paper, following O’Mahony & Karp (2022, SMJ)

Breadth: license permissiveness

Permissive MIT · BSD · Apache 2.0

Restrictive GPL family: GPL v2 · AGPL

Permissive licenses admit these users alongside all others, producing a wider and more diverse set of adopters.

Restrictive licenses exclude commercial and related users whose business models require proprietary distribution.

Benefit 1

Context-specific information

Each user holds context-specific information about performance and adaptation needs that is costly for the firm to acquire on its own.

Franke & von Hippel (2003); Lakhani & von Hippel (2003)

Benefit 2

Network effects

The more adopters a project has, the faster it improves and the more attractive it becomes to subsequent adopters.

Shapiro & Varian (1999); von Hippel & von Krogh (2003)

H1a: release under permissive licenses

Under the constraint

Firms depend more heavily on contributions from downstream users.

The license

The scale and diversity of these contributions depend on how permissive the license is.

Dependence

A wider user base expands the set of downstream relationships through which the firm reconfigures its dependence.

With ties to many downstream users, no single relationship carries the firm’s dependence, and the power imbalance falls.

Emerson (1962); Casciaro & Piskorski (2005)

Hypothesis 1aFollowing supply-side constraints on access to upstream hardware complement, software firms will increase their release of open source projects under permissive licenses.

Depth: gatekeeping openness

Closed gatekeepingonly the firm’s employees hold write access

Open gatekeepingexternal developers who have earned trust also hold it

Write access lets a developer

merge proposed changes into the main codebase

review contributions from others

extend these privileges to additional developers

Those without write access can propose changes, report issues and submit work for review, but cannot modify the codebase directly.

Open gatekeeping: the firm gives up exclusive control of its code.

Example: in Baidu’s PaddlePaddle, a Committer gets write access to the code repository after several merged pull requests and reviews and the approval of two Committers (community-membership.md, captured 13 Oct 2026).

Earning write access

Example · OpenClaw, MIT license

Started by one developer in November 2025, now stewarded by an independent foundation.

More than two dozen core maintainers hold write access, among them four from Nvidia, four from Microsoft, three from OpenAI and three from Tencent.

The New Stack, 9 Jul 2026; GitHub, openclaw/openclaw, read 14 Oct 2026

Outsiders earn write access by contributing steadily first: the “joining script” (von Krogh, Spaeth & Lakhani, 2003, Research Policy).

Firms can move a project from proprietary to collective governance (O’Mahony & Karp, 2022, Strategic Management Journal).

Write access goes to outside developers who have earned trust through sustained contribution.

H1b: use of external developers in gatekeeping

Signal 1

Democratic governance

Outside contributions have a credible pathway to shape the project’s direction.

O’Mahony & Ferraro (2007); O’Mahony & Karp (2022)

Signal 2

Labor market

Higher-ranked governance positions bring greater employability.

Hann, Roberts & Slaughter (2013); Xu, Nian & Cabral (2020)

Extending gatekeeper roles to external developers transforms a unilateral relationship into a distributed form of engagement: mutual dependence.

Gulati & Sytch (2007)

Hypothesis 1bFollowing supply-side constraints on access to upstream hardware complement, software firms will increase the use of external developers in gatekeeping their open source projects.

The private-collective model

Developers participate when the private returns to participation exceed the associated costs.

von Hippel (MIT) & von Krogh (ETH Zurich), Organization Science 14(2), 2003

  • 1Private investmentprotect the invention and keep the returnsopen source fits neither
  • 2Collective actiona public good, so everyone may free ride 
  • 3Private-collectivethose who write the code get returns that those who only download it do notour lens for H2

The paper’s four private returns

use and modify it for one’s own purposes

learning that translates into productivity

career signals from visible contributions and governance roles

access to external knowledge

H2a: governance changes facilitate community adoption

Licensing

Fewer legal constraints

Commercial users can integrate the technology into proprietary products.

Lerner & Tirole (2005); Stewart et al. (2006)

Gatekeeping

A more reliable technology

Open, democratic governance signals that the project will evolve in response to community needs.

O’Mahony & Ferraro (2007); O’Mahony & Karp (2022)

Why reuse at all: developers reuse code to add functionality quickly and to save time and cost (Haefliger, von Krogh & Spaeth 2008, Management Science).

Hypothesis 2aFollowing supply-side constraints on access to upstream hardware complement, software firms’ governance changes in open source projects will facilitate community adoption.

H2b: governance changes facilitate community contribution

Licensing

A larger pool

Permissive licensing enlarges the pool of users from which contributors can emerge.

Lerner & Tirole (2002)

Gatekeeping

A visible governance position

A career signal, and proof that contributions from outside the firm can shape the project.

Hann, Roberts & Slaughter (2013)

In two firm-sponsored projects, the sponsor’s credibility and openness raised volunteers’ identification with the community, and through it their intrinsic motivation (Spaeth, von Krogh & He 2015, ISR).

Hypothesis 2bFollowing supply-side constraints on access to upstream hardware complement, software firms’ governance changes in open source projects will facilitate community contribution.

Measuring gatekeeping

Merging needs write access. Recall the pull request on the GitHub basics page: a maintainer with write access merged a contributor’s branch.

StepWhat we do

2Identify peopleMatch pushers to Revelio employment spells (5,331 matched); email domains, company fields, bios
3Insider or outsiderCoded month by month; a push keeps access active for three months
4Measure1 if verified employees hold less than half of active write access, else 0

Contribution to resource dependence theory

Prior researchOur extension
The constraintOn one partnerEnvironmental-level: every advanced-chip supplier under the same rule
How it is rebalancedUpstream: absorption, countervailing, avoidanceDownstream: dependence reconfiguration
Emerson’s balancing operationNew partners of the same type, upstreamNew relationships with distributed users and developers, downstream

From concentrated supply-side dependence on a few players to distributed demand-side dependence. Licensing lowers the power imbalance; gatekeeping deepens mutual dependence.

“Upstream dependence can be rebalanced downstream.”

Liu, Tong & Li, building on Emerson’s (1962) “balancing operation”

Contributions

1Resource dependenceMotive: from supply to demandWhen the whole upstream is constrained at once, firms rebalance their dependence downstream. Dependence reconfiguration extends Emerson’s balancing operation from new suppliers to distributed users and developers.
2User innovation /
demand-based viewWhere the value comes fromPrior work explains firm-sponsored user innovation mainly through heterogeneous demand and sticky information. We add a supply-side driver: firms turn to demand-side value creation when a supply-side source of advantage is restricted.
3Open-source governanceProcess: breadth and depthFirms change how they organize innovation through licensing (breadth) and gatekeeping (depth). Each carries part of the effect to adoption and contribution.

Global South strategy: facing restricted access to Global North technology, firms can do more than adapt; they can rebalance their dependence downstream. China’s AI firms are our case.

Recent work: firms on the U.S. Entity List leaned more on science (Wang, Li & Wang, 2026, Science). We show firms also changed how they organize innovation, from concentrated supply-side dependence to distributed demand-side dependence.

Implication: restricting chips diffused code, through channels the rules do not reach.

Chips restricted.
Code released.

And governance shapes whether the community comes.

Backup index

More questions, short answers

Is it ChatGPT, not the controls?

India and Japan placebos and the triple differences against each, on B7.

Is write access governance?

Push rights are necessary to merge; robust to windows and a continuous share.

Do control firms (levels 1–2) react too?

That would make us underestimate the effect; dose-response.

Substantive innovation?

Forks and pull requests capture adoption and contribution; Hugging Face derivatives next.

Government push for open source?

Hard to separate fully; the timing tracks the controls, and the policy push is partly a response. Examples: E8.

Why October 2022, when A800/H800 stayed legal until October 2023?

The 2022 rule removed the frontier and signaled a moving boundary; event-study timing.

Gitee migration?

Moves show up as zeros, which would make us underestimate the effect.

Investor signaling (Conti, Peukert & Roche 2025)?

Signaling would predict a stronger response among VC-backed firms; treatment × VC backing was not significant (p > 0.20, March exploration), and signaling does not explain giving up exclusive control of the code.

Mostly zeros: are log coefficients percentages?

Not exactly. Under Poisson (PPML), licensing (+0.76, p = .01) and new repositories (+0.66, p = .03) hold. Forks are positive but imprecise (p = .14) and external PRs are flat. The community response shows up as more firms getting any fork or outside PR (+3.3 pp each, p = .05 and .08).

Backup index

Caveats on the open-source boom

1

The point gap between the best open and the best closed models has not shrunk in 2026.

Arena: 0.5% in Aug 2024, about 3.4% in early 2026. Epoch ECI gap: about 9–11 points.

2

Some 2026 Chinese flagships are less open.

Kimi K3, MiniMax M3 and GLM-5.3 use custom licenses; Alibaba’s top Qwen models are API-only.

3

Downloads are not deployments.

The top 200 models account for 49.6% of Hugging Face downloads; OpenRouter is one platform.

Reply

Apache or MIT, among Chinese releases above 20B parameters in 2026: the base of the ecosystem remains overwhelmingly permissive.

Partial re-closing at the very top fits the cost–benefit logic once capability catches up. More counter-evidence: E14.

Hugging Face, “State of Open Models, Summer 2026” (14 Aug 2026); Arena; Epoch AI, Capabilities Index.

Backup index

Hardware and software: complements or substitutes?

We measure how firms organize innovation; substitution in the input mix may also have occurred.

DeepSeek-AI, DeepSeek-V4 report (released Apr 2026); shown: the arXiv copy 2606.19348 (Jun 2026), Sec. 3.1, p. 16. PDF link border removed; highlight added.

What our data show
  • Governance opens: permissive releases +7 log points, open gatekeeping +15.7 pp.
  • Governance carries 10–40% of the community effect (mediation; descriptive).
  • The response rises with AI exposure for gatekeeping, forks and pull requests (B11).

Longer version: B1. From the field: E1, E3.

Teece’s logic is part of the story: losing compute lowers the value of keeping code closed. Resource dependence adds how firms organize the outsiders they now depend on.

Effects: paper, Tables 3 and 4 (single-mediator shares 10.3–39.6%); dose-response: replication package, Table A6. Paper, pp. 11 and 36; Teece (1986).

Backup index

How did we classify AI firms? Are these model companies?

Mostly not. The treated group is the broader AI software sector, and most are AI application firms.

About 89% of treated firms (127 of 143) are AI application firms; foundation-model developers are 3 firms.

How we classified: an LLM (Qwen3 8B) coded each firm’s 2022 Crunchbase profile on the 1–5 ladder, so post-shock rebranding can’t move a firm into treatment; manual review of 1,974 firms: 99.6% agree on treatment.

Paper, Appendix A; firms per level: replication data, matched sample (664 firms).

Backup index

Do Hugging Face and GitHub really give firms a feedback channel?

Yes. On both, outsiders can propose changes and the firm decides what to merge.

GitHub, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3, merged pull requests; captured 13 Oct 2026.

  • GitHub: all 25 merged pull requests on DeepSeek-V3 came from 21 accounts outside the organization.
  • Hugging Face: since 25 May 2022 every model repo has a Community tab where anyone can open a pull request; the owner merges it.
  • The caveat: much Hugging Face traffic is noise, one reason our measures come from GitHub’s monthly event record.

GitHub, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 merged pull requests (read 13 Oct 2026); huggingface.co/blog/community-update (25 May 2022); Hugging Face Hub docs.

Backup index

Can firms in China even use GitHub?

Yes. GitHub is reachable from China, if often slowly; it is Hugging Face that is blocked.

  • China blocked GitHub once, for three days (21–23 Jan 2013), and lifted the block after a public outcry.
  • More than 11 million developers in China use GitHub (11.35M, 2026 Q1), third after the U.S. and India.
  • Hugging Face has been blocked in mainland China since 2023.
  • A move to Gitee would show up as zeros in our data, so it would make us underestimate the effect (B13).

GreatFire (Jan 2013); GitHub Innovation Graph (2026 Q1); Semafor (20 Oct 2023); TechCrunch (21 Aug 2020) and The Register (20 May 2022) on Gitee.

Backup index

Was there an equivalent supplier to switch to?

AI firms had no equivalent supplier to switch to, could not merge across the border, and could not exit AI. The whole upstream was constrained at once.

Eric Xu, Huawei · September 2025

“The Chinese mainland will lag behind in semiconductor manufacturing process nodes for a relatively long time.”

Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA · October 2025

“We went from a 95% market share to 0%.”

DeepSeek, ISCA ’25 paper · June 2025

“due to policy and regulatory constraints, just over two thousand GPUs were ultimately deployed.”

Partial workaroundIts limit
China-specific A800 and H800Legal until 17 Oct 2023; H800 NVLink cut from 900 to 400 GB/s
H20License required from 9 Apr 2025; reversed Jul 2025
Renting U.S. chips in the cloudReported Aug 2024; “not a violation of U.S. regulations”
SmugglingOne case: at least $160M of H100 and H200 GPUs, Oct 2024 – May 2025

Some firms found partial workarounds, so our treated firms were less constrained than a full cutoff would imply; if anything we underestimate the response to a binding constraint.

Xu: Huawei Connect keynote (18 Sept 2025). Huang: Citadel Securities, via Wccftech (17 Oct 2025). DeepSeek, ISCA ’25, Secs. 4.1, 5.1. BIS (17 Oct 2023); NVIDIA 8-K (9 Apr 2025); Bloomberg (15 Jul 2025); Reuters (23 Aug 2024); U.S. Department of Justice (8 Dec 2025).

Examples from the field

Recent studies and where ours sits

Wang, Li & Wang (2026)
Science		After U.S. Entity List designation, firms filed 72% more domestic science-linked patents; we show firms also changed how they organize innovation.
Chen et al. (2026)
SSRN		Sanctioned firms filed about as many patents as before, but of lower quality; we look at open code and the community around it.
Haese & Peukert (2025)
Management Science		One firm moves onto an open foundation (Edge onto Chromium); our firms open their own code and governance after a supply shock.
Hoffmann, Nagle & Zhou (2024)
HBS working paper		$4.15B of supply-side value, $8.8T of demand-side value: most of the value is created in use, and our firms come to depend on those users.
Nagle & Yue (2025)
SSRN draft		Open models took about 20% of tokens but 4% of revenue; we study how firms organize the outsiders they then depend on.

Wang, Li & Wang, Science 393, 1196–1199 (2026), DOI 10.1126/science.aed7991; Chen, Ding, He, Wang, Xia & Yao, SSRN 7118620 (2026); Haese & Peukert, Management Science (2025), DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2023.02886, and ProMarket (16 Dec 2025); Hoffmann, Nagle & Zhou, HBS WP 24-038 (2024); Nagle & Yue, SSRN 5767103 (18 Nov 2025).

Examples from the field

Counter-evidence: tighter licenses at the very top, possible Chinese limits, licenses that exclude regions

Tightening at the very top fits the dependence logic, and the paper codes license type, not “open” as one thing.

Tighter licenses at the very topKimi K3 needs a separate agreement when a licensee’s revenue “exceeds 20 million US dollars.” Our window ends Oct 2025; 81% of large Chinese releases in 2026 stay Apache or MIT.
Possible Chinese limitsChina’s Commerce Ministry (MOFCOM) is consulting; “No final implementation date has been announced” (Tech Times, citing the FT and Reuters). Proposals only.
Licenses that exclude regionsTencent Hunyuan-A13B: “THIS LICENSE AGREEMENT DOES NOT APPLY IN THE EUROPEAN UNION, UNITED KINGDOM AND SOUTH KOREA.”

huggingface.co: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 and tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct license files; Tech Times (22 Jul 2026), citing Reuters and the FT; Hugging Face, “State of Open Models, Summer 2026.”

China’s share of GitHub AI contributions is undercounted

Contributions to AI projects on GitHub

AI Index 2025 estimate, by IP geolocation

Why the 2% is low, and why our measure is unaffected

IP geolocation undercounts Chinese developers, who often use VPNs.

The paper measures firm-owned GitHub organizations, matched by firm, so it does not depend on IP location.

Examples from the field

Open questions

Persistence

A durable change in how firms organize innovation, or a tactical pivot that reverses once hardware access returns?

We do not observe performance or hardware substitution.

Direction of innovation

future research

We plan to measure whether the direction of their innovation changes.

Bargaining power

Can de facto software standards strengthen these firms’ position with hardware suppliers?

The state

How much of the openness reflects government support for open source, itself partly a response to the controls? (Jin et al., 2026)

Other chokepoints

Biotech tools, chipmaking equipment, critical minerals.

Where output is physical, firms would need other ways to manage their dependence.
